context: Single-view 2D density contour heatmap overlaid on a scatter plot of 8,000 points from 3 bivariate normal clusters; supports brush-to-zoom with contour recomputation at the zoomed scale.
first_impression: Immediately readable — three spatially distinct clusters pop against the dark background, and the viridis density gradient communicates intensity without clutter.
what_works: The dual encoding (categorical scatter points + sequential viridis contours) is well-separated perceptually: cluster membership and density intensity are two different visual channels that don't fight each other. Cluster separation is large enough that structure is legible at a glance with no interaction required.
what_doesnt: Running two simultaneous color systems (3 categorical tolColors on points + viridis on contours) creates a momentary ambiguity — a viewer may wonder whether the contour hue corresponds to the legend entries before realizing it encodes density, not category. Axis labels ('X' / 'Y') are generic placeholders that reduce interpretive grounding. Animation quality on brush-to-zoom cannot be assessed from a static screenshot.
